dedupe_keys.name: household energy retrofit behavior herb agent based model

description: HERB simulates how homeowners in a neighbourhood decide to retrofit their homes for energy. Technical factors such as the home's energy standard, available subsidies and neighbours' retrofits are turned into psychological variables, perceived comfort gain, worry about cost and seeing the home as wasteful, which move households through four decision stages taken from a large population survey in Norway. Retrofits change the home and influence friends and neighbours, and energy standards decline over time so households must retrofit again. It was published by Lars Even Egner on CoMSES in October 2022; experiment data of about 15 GB are in DataverseNO under doi:10.18710/XOSAMD. Coverage: stylised Norwegian neighbourhoods. Access: free NetLogo code on CoMSES. Licence: GPL-3.0. Caveats: behaviour rules come from one country's survey. Simulation uses are testing subsidy and information policies for residential retrofit rates in building stock scenarios. Related records: the NIER retrofit model and CEDSS.
inputs: Neighbourhood of households with energy standards and subsidies
Stage model of retrofit decisions from a Norwegian survey
name: Household Energy Retrofit Behavior (HERB) agent-based model
outputs: Retrofit adoption and energy standard of homes over time
